sources.citation: d'Orbigny, Alcide (1839). Voyage dans l'Amérique méridionale, t. IV, 1re partie: L'homme américain (de l'Amérique méridionale) considéré sous ses rapports physiologiques et moraux. Paris: Pitois-Levrault. 'Nation Canichana', pp. 300-301; comparative remarks on Moxos languages pp. 284-285.
sources.note: p. 301: the language 'est musicale, fortement accentuée, quelquefois dure à entendre, à cause des sons gutturaux et des sons composés de plusieurs consonnes unies'; nearly all words end in vowels, with hard exceptions in -ac, -ec, -ip, -ij, -ch. Impressionistic; gives no stress position. General chapter (p. 74) says all American languages are 'fortement accentuées'.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Canichana language' (en) and 'Idioma canichana' (es), wikitext retrieved 2026-09-17; grammar sketch and phoneme tables cited to Crevels 2012.
sources.note: Second-hand summary of Crevels 2012: tentative 5-vowel and ~20-consonant inventory (with parenthesised ejectives), nominal/verbal morphology, syntax. No mention of acento/stress anywhere.

sources.citation: Fabre, Alain (2005-; entry revised 20 Nov 2015). Diccionario etnolingüístico y guía bibliográfica de los pueblos indígenas sudamericanos: KANICHANA.
sources.note: Bibliographic guide only: 'Es de lamentar la inexistencia de estudios lingüísticos modernos sobre el kanichana, que obliga a recurrir a los materiales ya antiguos publicados por Créqui-Montfort & Rivet (1913-14)'; lists Crevels 2002, 2012, Montaño Aragón 1987, Ibarra Grasso 1982. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Créqui-Montfort, Georges de & Paul Rivet (1913). Linguistique bolivienne. La langue Kaničana. Mémoires de la Société de Linguistique de Paris 18: 354-377.
sources.note: Full offprint (24 pp.) read. No phonetic or accent section; p. 355: 'Il y a très peu d'indications morphologiques ou grammaticales à tirer des éléments dont nous disposons'; for their transcription they refer to their Otuki paper (JSA 1913: 318 n. 2). Grammar notes (pp. 355-364) cover gender, number, prefixes, suffixes, pronouns, conjugation, negation only; vocabulary (pp. 365-376) reproduces d'Orbigny/Heath/Cardús/Teza forms with sporadic acute/circumflex marks (ni-kôma, ni-tuxû, eu-kôro, enko-phurûnue) that are never explained. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Heath, Edwin R. (1883). Dialects of Bolivian Indians. A philological contribution from material gathered during three years residence in the Department of Beni, in Bolivia. Kansas City Review of Science and Industry 6(12): 679-687.
sources.note: 165-word comparative list incl. Canichana (corrected by 'Don Hugo Boger'); only orthographic note: 'The sounds of the vowels and letters are after the rules of the Spanish language.' No accent statement; the scanned of the Canichana column shows no accent marks.

sources.citation: Teza, Emilio (1868). Saggi inediti di lingue americane. Appunti bibliografici. Annali delle Università Toscane 10 (Pisa), 117-163; Canisiana Pater/Ave/Credo at p. 139 (offprint pp. 40-42).
sources.note: Untranslated mission texts copied from a manuscript ('lengua de la nacion canisianà... del pueblo de S. Pedro'); no linguistic commentary, nothing on accent.

sources.citation: Crevels, Mily (2012). Canichana. In M. Crevels & P. Muysken (eds.), Lenguas de Bolivia, tomo II: Amazonía, 415-449. La Paz: Plural Editores. ISBN 978-99954-1-475-5.

sources.note: The only modern descriptive sketch (Glottolog's sole descriptive ref); has a phonology section (tentative phoneme inventories per Wikipedia summary) and, being based on old wordlists with accent marks plus Crevels' 1999-2001 fieldwork with rememberers and GlobalRecordings audio, is the one place a statement on accent/stress could exist.
